newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. expresses concern over Jerusalem project.
newsitem.headline: U.S. expresses concern over Jerusalem project.

text.p: The United States expressed concern on Wednesday over Israeli plans to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem, a move that a U.S. diplomat said could lead to violence.

Edward Abington, U.S. Consul General in Jerusalem, told a news conference that construction of thousands of Jewish homes on Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel, and other settlement activity would create a "very, very volatile situation".

He said the United States sent messages to Israel and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat that "we do not want to see any violence" after an Israeli ministerial committee on Jerusalem approves the project.

Abington was speaking at the Palestinian Information Ministry in the West Bank, hours before the Israeli committee convened amid warnings by Palestinians of possible violence over what they view as an attempt by Israel to cement its hold over all of Jerusalem.

"We do not want to see a situation which could get out of control. I think that one thing that was clear from the events of last September, if violence does occur, the outcome can be very dangerous, and violence can be very difficult to control," Abington said.

The diplomat was referring to Palestinian-Israeli clashes that erupted after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened a new entrance to an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy places in East Jerusalem. Sixty-one Arabs and 15 Israeli soldiers died.
Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state. Israel says all of the city is its "eternal" capital, a claim not recognised internationally.
PLO-Israeli peace deals left the sensitive issue of the fate of Jerusalem for talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip which must be completed by 1999.

Reiterating Washington's position on Jerusalem, Abington said: "I think we have consistently said there is no issue that is more sensitive or more volatile than the issue of Jerusalem, we have said we do not want to see actions that would increase the possibility of violence."
The U.S. official declined to say how Washington would react if Israel went ahead with plans to build a new Jewish neighbourhoood in Jabal Abu Ghneim.
"An authoritative reaction has to come from Washington," he said.
